text: A linter checks style and convention — how your code is written. A static analyzer reasons about what your code actually does, flagging patterns associated with real vulnerabilities.
forge fmt check was already in Lesson 8's workflow. Solhint goes further — security rules like flagging timestamp reliance, and style rules like explicit visibility and naming conventions.
A multi-job pipeline should order cheapest and fastest first. needs colon lint means the expensive test job doesn't even start until the cheap lint job passes — fail fast, save CI minutes.
Solhint's security-category rules are a cheap preview of what heavier tools check in depth — they catch the obvious, but don't trace actual control and data flow.
Linting is the fast, cheap first gate. Lesson 10 adds the gate that actually reasons about vulnerability patterns — Slither and Mythril, in the same pipeline.
